messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: High latency alert: /v1/generate p95 increased from ~220ms to 1.8s across us-east-1 pool. Auto-impact: 12% of requests >2s. Metric: infra.latency.p95 > 1.5s.
Alex: acked — paging oncall now.
Oncall-Bot: Paging Priya (oncall). Escalation: three pagers.
Priya: I'm on it, joining. quick ask: any recent infra pushes?
Samir: Rolled kernel image to workers-last-night on a small canary pool, tag: kernel-6.1.9-rc. Only 10% at 02:10 UTC.
Lia: Noted. I see ramp in p95 starting ~02:45 UTC correlating with general rollout window.
Alex: timeline assembly: can we collect perf counters and top-of-runqueue snapshots?
Priya: grabbing traces + perf from affected hosts now.
Samir: sharing initial trace bundle: https://internal.artifacts/trace-bundle/4681234567.tar.gz
Priya: paste of critical spans (summarized):
```
span: req_id=aa12, service=inference-runtime, op=decode, duration=1.2s
span: kernel-sched-wait, duration=0.45s, stack: schedule, try_to_wake, pick_next_task
span: gpu-copy, duration=0.05s
```

Priya: perf stat (host i-0abc):
```
0.00% cycles:u
+ 32% cpu-idle -> much lower CPU busy?
context-switches: +41000 (baseline 8k)
runqueue_length avg: 6.2 (baseline 0.6)
```

Lia: runqueue and context-switch spike consistent with kernel scheduling stalls.
Alex: Are requests being batched more? batching config unchanged. Could be more tail due to preempt latency.
Samir: kernel-6.1.9-rc included a preempt path tweak (CONFIG_PREEMPTION=full) plus a scheduler patch backported. Might explain longer pick_next_task times under our workload.
Priya: Hypothesis A: recent kernel change increased scheduler latency under high socket/wake contention -> p95 regression.
Priya: Hypothesis B: downstream change in runtime causing lock convoys on KV cache leading to scheduler pressure.
Alex: Need to rule out runtime lock: can we get blocked-locks from strace/futex stats?
Samir: futex_waiters shows small bump but not enough to explain 1s stalls. Kernel traces show long schedule() stacks.
Lia: Correlate by host: affected hosts all on kernel-6.1.9-rc tag. Canary hosts on 6.1.8 stable show no spike.
Oncall-Bot: Customer impact: 18 seats with sustained error/timeout risk; SLOs degraded. Notifying CS for impacted accounts.
Alex: Mitigation plan: 1) Stop kernel rollout (paused) 2) Roll back canary to 6.1.8 on affected hosts 3) Add temporary routing rule to reduce batch size to 1 for critical customers 4) Collect deeper perf counters for 6.1.9 vs 6.1.8.
Priya: Executing rollback on canary now (hosts: i-0abc, i-0def, i-0fed). Command run:
```
ansible-playbook rollback-kernel.yml -l canary -e kernel_version=6.1.8-stable
```

Samir: Rollback in progress. ETA ~4m per host to reboot and rejoin.
Priya: After one host rebooted back to 6.1.8 p95 samples dropped from 1.7s -> 320ms for that host's shard.
Lia: Nice. That strongly points to kernel delta.
Alex: Keep rolling back until canary fully reverted, then hold rollout and open kernel regression ticket with kernel patch set and bisect plan.
Oncall-Bot: Noted mitigation and customer notifications.
Priya: Collecting perf counters for both kernels now; dumping trace span comparisons.
Samir: Also observed increased 'sched_migration' counts in 6.1.9 nodes. Copying kernel logs:
```
[  123.456789] task schedule: D stack_trace: schedule+0x45/0x70 pick_next_task_fair+0x1a0/0x360
[  123.456799] preempt_schedule: latency 480ms
```

Priya: Trace compare (6.1.9 vs 6.1.8) shows median decode span similar but 99th jumps from 0.45s -> 1.6s. p50 largely unchanged.
Alex: So p50 stable, p95 and p99 shifted = classic tail-regression. Good to call out in RCA.
Lia: Any evidence of network packet drops between runtime and GPU? I/O stats look normal.
Samir: No NIC errors. GPU times unchanged. Kernel scheduling is the main signal.
Priya: Customer impact note for post-incident summary: some latency-sensitive customers hit retries and degraded UX; no data loss. CS will follow up with advisories.
Alex: Next actions:
- Samir: open kernel-bisect ticket and include trace bundles + perf diffs (assign to kernel-team).
- Priya: compile timeline + mitigation notes for postmortem (include commands, exact host IDs, times).
- Lia: run synthetic workload on 6.1.9 vs 6.1.8 to reproduce at scale and attach perf counter graphs.

Priya: Quick status: canary rollback finished, p95 overall reduced to 260ms cluster-wide, autoscaling stable.
Samir: Filed ticket KERN-8472 with initial hypothesis and link to traces.
Lia: I'll schedule a debug session w/ kernel team and runtime team in 2h to walk through stacks.
Alex: Thanks all. I'll draft the incident summary and the initial RCA skeleton.
Oncall-Bot: Incident state: Mitigated -> Monitoring. Please update when transition to postmortem.
Priya: Adding final notes: root cause suspected = scheduler regression introduced in kernel-6.1.9-rc under our workload; manifested as increased runqueue and long schedule latencies -> p95/p99 tail increase. Mitigation = rollback to 6.1.8 and pause rollout.
Alex: End thread — we'll continue postmortem in #eng-sre. :thumbsup:
